video_title: Minnesota Timberwolves offseason plans: Giannis, Julius Randle and more

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Wolfson on Timberwolves' need for a superstar and roster changes
quotes.excerpt: Roster changes need to come for this team to have a fighting chance the next couple years.
quotes.quote: Yes on will, yes on should. There is a ceiling on this roster. The Wolves realize that. Tim Connelly realized it last summer making a push for Kevin Durant. I foresee roster changes coming. Nothing has changed on my front. We've talked about this for multiple months. They are not firing the head coach. Chris Finch has multiple years, two years left on his contract. First off, Alex Rodriguez and Marc Lore are not cutting the big fat check to Chris Finch for millions of dollars to go away. But even so, those guys are big believers in Chris Finch. So roster changes need to come for this team to have a fighting chance the next couple years. Yes, they want to be in the Eastern Conference, but that's still a few years out if it even happens. So for the next few years, how do you compete with the Spurs and Thunder? You need another superstar. They would love to acquire Giannis.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis's leverage and Minnesota's appeal as a trade destination
quotes.excerpt: Giannis has the hammer because he's essentially in a contract year. Wherever he goes, he's signing an extension.
quotes.quote: Let's not forget, Phil, Giannis has the hammer because he's essentially in a contract year. There's that player option, but wherever he goes, he's signing an extension. I could certainly concoct a great package that the Portland Trail Blazers could put together for Giannis. But if Giannis through his representation signals to the Blazers, I'm not signing a contract extension, you're not giving up Scoot Henderson and a million draft picks. You're just not doing that. The word is, going back to February, Giannis has interest in a few places. I was told, I was led to believe that Minnesota is one of those places, that there is enough intrigue, Giannis teaming up with Anthony Edwards. So yes, I absolutely foresee Tim Connelly re-engaging the Bucks, maybe already has.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaden McDaniels's inclusion is essential for a Giannis trade
quotes.excerpt: You're not getting Giannis without including Jaden McDaniels.

text_blocks.speaker: Judd
text_blocks.text: All right, let's explore the space some more then. What does a Giannis trade look like?

text_blocks.speaker: Darren Wolfson
text_blocks.text: Well, I mean, I brought that up with Bobby Marks on Monday. I trust Bobby Marks's opinion wholeheartedly. He told me, you're not getting Giannis without including Jaden McDaniels. I get it. You're thinking about Julius Randle, plus Rudy Gobert, plus okay, you part with Terrance Shannon Jr., TJ Shannon, plus your 26th first-round pick, pick 28, plus your 2033 first-round pick, which is tradable as of the draft next month, plus okay, pick swap in a couple years. You can offer a pick swap in 28. Okay, you're putting that all on the table, but the idea is you want to keep Jaden McDaniels. I understand that. I just don't know, Judd, how you trump a Miami offer of Khalil Ware, Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez, a bunch of draft picks, better draft picks. I just don't know how the Bucks say Minnesota, I'm accepting your offer, Miami, I'm not accepting your offer when you're not getting Jaden McDaniels. So I just, I believe, I don't have this like 100% nailed down, but I just don't see the pathway. Bobby Marks is in agreement. I just don't see it, he doesn't see it, how you acquire Giannis without parting ways with Jaden McDaniels.

quotes.speaker: Phil
quotes.summary_phrase: The "nuke button" trade for Giannis requires multiple key players and picks
quotes.excerpt: You hit the nuke button and you just try to put the two best superstars out there, old school style.
quotes.quote: I think what makes this so nuclear and I'm not even like I'm very 50/50 on whether this would actually work, but you have two ways to really try to close the gap between San Antonio and Oklahoma City. A marginal tweak where you swap out let's say Julius for whether it's a Kyrie or whatever, and then hope that like Banchero takes a big step, TJ Shannon, Anthony Edwards that you've got enough collectively where the whole thing grows. Jaden gets better, Naz grows. Or you hit the nuke button and you just try to put the two best superstars out there, old school style, and hope that they can take on the depth and the waves that Oklahoma City and San Antonio send at you. But in a Giannis trade, because of his value and how much money he makes, and you have to come close to matching salaries, and because I don't think he can play next to Gobert, you're talking about Gobert, Randle, and Jaden McDaniels for sure for value purposes and salary matching and roster construction purposes, plus whoever you draft with the 28th overall pick on behalf of somebody else, like once that pick is made, then you can trade it, right? That's the way it works. And then a couple other like a pick swap later in the 2023 first-round pick, plus a couple other younger pieces, what would you have left around those two superstars? You'd probably be then taking back like Miles Turner from the Bucks so that you'd have at least like a stretch five, take his salary off of the Bucks' hands. I've seen iterations that involve that as well. But you would be completely nuking, and I think most people are fine with nuking the Rudy Gobert and Julius Randle part of it.

quotes.speaker: Phil
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis trade hinges on Jaden McDaniels, health, and contract extension
quotes.excerpt: You're not completing this trade without including Jaden McDaniels.
quotes.quote: But it's the Jaden McDaniels part, I agree with Duggy. You're not completing this trade with other teams offering decent packages without including Jaden McDaniels. And then you're hoping that A, Giannis stays healthy, B, doesn't go over the age cliff, because he is in his early 30s, and C, that he signs a long-term extension with you, which would probably be a prerequisite before you'd ever pull the trigger. So there's a ton of factors involved with making this happen, Dukes.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis has multiple preferred destinations, not just Minnesota
quotes.excerpt: I'm not under the impression that it's Minnesota or bust for Giannis.
quotes.quote: Yeah, wherever Giannis is going, he's signing an extension, right? Like Kevin Durant gets traded to the Rockets, signs an extension, right? So that would be worked out beforehand. So you would know once you acquire Giannis, the extension will get done. But yeah, I'm not under the impression that it's Minnesota or bust for Giannis. Like that would be the ideal scenario if Giannis just said, I want to go to Minnesota. You have to send me to Minnesota. I have the hammer, so Milwaukee, I'm leaving you after the year. So you have a choice. Get whatever you can get from Minnesota, or I'm leaving, I'm not exercising my player option, I'm leaving next summer. But I'm not under the impression, Phil, it's Minnesota or bust. I believe Giannis is interested in like three or four, maybe five destinations. But does Minnesota fall under that? Yeah. I think there's genuine interest in Giannis teaming up with Anthony Edwards. So, okay, let's play this out. You have Naz still, you have Giannis, you have Ant, but yeah, what does the rest of the roster look like? Let's say Shannon is going out and Jaden is going out.

quotes.speaker: Phil
quotes.summary_phrase: A hypothetical four-team trade sends Jaden, Julius, and picks for Giannis and Miles Turner
quotes.excerpt: The Wolves would send out Jaden, Julius, to the Bucks and also whoever they... their 28th overall pick this year.

text_blocks.speaker: Darren Wolfson
text_blocks.text: I guess here's the question. I've not seen examples where Miles Turner also ends up here. What is that contract?

text_blocks.speaker: Darren Wolfson
text_blocks.text: Because he signed a monster contract, right?

text_blocks.speaker: Phil
text_blocks.text: Yeah. He's 30 years old. By the way, like still a really effective shot blocker and three-point shooting big man who is he's the perfect I see what the Bucks' vision was because he's the perfect type of five to play next to Giannis who does not have a lot of range beyond, you know, 10 or 15 feet. And Miles Turner, who yeah, turns 30 for this upcoming season, it's 26 and a half, 27.8, and then a $29 million player option. And our guy, our friend Tim Garrison, notable Wolves Twitter guy who does a great job like putting together kind of salary cap related discussions and he studies it hardcore, yeah, he's very good. He does a really good job. And again, this is just like it's just one idea for a package here. But the Wolves would essentially send out, he put this out on Twitter yesterday. The Wolves would send out Jaden, Julius, to the Bucks and also whoever they I don't know exactly where it's like a four-team trade. They would send out their 28th overall pick this year after they make it because you have to wait, you have to make a pick in you can't have back-to-back years without a pick.

quotes.speaker: Phil
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gobert to Hornets, Giannis and Miles Turner to Timberwolves, Dante DiVincenzo for salary matching
quotes.excerpt: Coming back to the Timberwolves would be Giannis, Miles Turner, and then I believe from the Clippers, Derrick Jones Jr.
quotes.quote: Go to the Hornets who need rim protection and some size and to raise their defensive floor. And then coming back to the Timberwolves would be Giannis, Miles Turner, and then I believe from the Clippers, Derrick Jones Jr. would be routed as part of a four-team trade that includes them. This would almost have to be a four like a three, four or five-team trade because the Wolves and Bucks don't necessarily match up perfectly and like or you could send some things to the Bucks and then they could reroute like Rudy for a couple picks over here and take on some expiring contracts, whatever. I also think, I'll throw this out, I think this is the summer to trade Dante DiVincenzo because it's an expiring contract. He's almost certainly not going to be available until the very end of the season. So if you can use his $12 million to like salary match and bring in a player that's going to be healthy.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Dante DiVincenzo's trade value and the complexity of multi-team deals
quotes.excerpt: I think it's more likely you use that expiring contract as a piece. Man, four-team trades... are they tough.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I mean, I brought up with Bobby the possibility of a disabled player's exception for Dante, which would be 50% of a salary, so approximately six and a half million, but he would have to be deemed out for the year. And like those disabled player exceptions, Bobby said, are so incredibly rare. Like Dante could be back late March, early April, like Jayson Tatum came back in season. It's possible, like okay, no on January or February, but latter part, like very latter part of the regular season or early portion of the playoffs, why can't Dante come back? So yeah, I agree. I think it's more likely you use that expiring contract as a piece. Man, four-team trades. I'm not saying they're impossible, Phil, but man alive, are they tough.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gobert is a Hall of Famer and floor raiser, but not a championship-winning centerpiece
quotes.excerpt: If Rudy Gobert is playing 30 to 35 minutes a night, you're not winning a championship.
quotes.quote: Charlotte is interesting. I mean, they have Kalkbrenner. They have another big, is it Diabate, Diabate? I might be botching the pronunciation, but you would think Charlotte is ready to take that next step. And like we know, Gobert raises the floor. Like Gobert easily a Hall of Famer, right? Like no debate whatsoever. I just I've always come to the conclusion, if Rudy Gobert is playing 30 to 35 minutes a night, you're not winning a championship. I've thought that for years, I continue to think that, but he's an incredible floor raiser. Like if you're Charlotte, he would be great. If you're New Orleans, think about hiring defensive-minded head coach Jamal Mosley. What about New Orleans for Gobert? Toronto. They were good, but Jakob Poeltl, like no. Toronto's had interest in Gobert for a while. Chicago too, but I don't know exactly what Chicago's thinking, they just hired a new front office. But like you can trade Rudy Gobert.

quotes.speaker: Judd
quotes.summary_phrase: Julius Randle's contract is tradable, and Spurs/Thunder success drives Wolves' urgency
quotes.excerpt: I can promise you, they can find a taker for Julius Randle.

text_blocks.speaker: Darren Wolfson
text_blocks.text: And you can absolutely trade Julius Randle. That was the word, Phil, when they re-signed him last summer. He's at 33 million give or take a couple hundred thousand dollars, then he has what, the player option, two years out at like 35, 35 and a half million dollars. Very tradable contract. I can promise you, they can find a taker for Julius Randle. I don't foresee a scenario where they have to add sweeteners to move off the Randle contract, put it that way.

text_blocks.speaker: Judd
text_blocks.text: So if Connelly and we know for a fact that he did try to get Durant a year ago because he had some concerns about his roster construction, as we now embark on watching the Spurs and Thunder play, and it's just become quite clear that they are the two best teams. How much more do you think that that drives not just him, but also A-Rod, Lore, and everyone at the top of the food chain with the Wolves to say, we've got a nice team, but it appears we're not going to be able to compete with those teams unless we make a move, and dare I say, I think a drastic move is probably correct. I don't know if the Wolves I don't know if they make a small move or a move that's considered to be, oh, that's interesting. I don't know that puts you in the tax bracket that we're now seeing the Thunder and Spurs playing.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Satisfying Anthony Edwards is crucial to prevent him from wanting to leave
quotes.excerpt: The fear is there that if you don't elevate to where Ant wants to go... Ant is off the charts.
quotes.quote: Yeah, it's absolutely motivating. My understanding is, when talking about ownership, 1A on the important scale, Anthony Edwards, 1B, Tim Connelly. So they'll give Tim Connelly a new contract this offseason, but it's about satisfying Anthony Edwards. And I get it, Ant has multiple years left on his contract. But trust me, the fear is there that if you don't elevate to where Ant wants to go, like competitive spirit-wise, Ant is off the charts. He really is. I don't even hold what we saw in Game 6 against him going to congratulate the Spurs with eight and a half minutes left, just knowing what he was gutting through. I can't quantify, we talked about this last week, I don't know if he's 70%, 75%, but we know with the knees, nowhere near 100%. I just I was thoroughly impressed with Ant even though I thought he had more in him heading into Game 5 coming off the Game 4 performance. But it's about satisfying Ant. The fear is, Judd, that at some point, does Ant through his representation, Bill Duffy and others, signal a desire to be elsewhere? We are nowhere near that point, but the fear is there. And so yeah, so Ant, I'm sure deep down knows that he can't get to where he wants to get to with this roster.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs and Thunder are dominant, requiring luck or injury setbacks to overcome
quotes.excerpt: What a freaking conundrum trying to overcome not one but both those teams for the next couple years.
quotes.quote: Now, I will also say, maybe it's just recency bias coming off last night, but man alive on the Spurs, right? And I still think that series is going minimum six, I think seven. I think SGA, Chet, and AJ Mitchell will play better as the series goes on. But how about Dylan Harper last night? 47 minutes, one turnover? Dude. That team is unbelievable. No De'Aaron Fox now. Castle had a bunch of turnovers, so if Fox plays those minutes, maybe the Spurs don't have as many turnovers, but like Dylan Harper playing all those minutes, like if Fox eats up some of those minutes, I don't know if the Spurs win. That's how good Dylan Harper is. I still wonder about De'Aaron Fox's future in San Antonio. We saw that big, big hug Fox with Ant. I just don't know if the Spurs would trade De'Aaron Fox here. If there's not a pathway to Giannis, could you go get De'Aaron Fox? I still wonder in the next couple years, what do the Spurs do with De'Aaron Fox? But just thinking about how good Harper is, then the rest of that roster, then knowing how good OKC is, what a freaking conundrum trying to overcome not one but both those teams for the next couple years. You need some luck, right? You need you're never going to root for some sort of injury, even on the minor scale, certainly never root for some sort of catastrophic injury, but like you would need one of those stars to have some sort of injury setback in early April heading into the postseason. If those rosters are fully healthy, I don't know how you beat either of those teams.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Wolves' locker room moodiness and Julius Randle's "nauseating" lack of effort
quotes.excerpt: The visual evidence of the lack of effort from Julius Randle on Friday... was nauseating.

text_blocks.speaker: Phil
text_blocks.text: What are your thoughts on the Wolves' locker room? Connelly, Naz Reid, Anthony Edwards with some cryptic like no comments, talking about moodiness and low basketball IQ. Just a lot more openness from that locker room voicing frustrations. No individual names were called out, we can make assumptions, but that's that's like the probably the most vocal that collectively they've been after a disappointing end to a season.

text_blocks.speaker: Darren Wolfson
text_blocks.text: I agree. Now low basketball IQ. How long have we discussed that? That's not breaking news. We've discussed that for a long time. This is not a smart IQ basketball team. It's just not. I mean, I thought Jay Williams, the former Duke point guard, had the brief run in the NBA before injuries derailed his pro career. He was on First Take on Monday with the visual evidence of the lack of effort from Julius Randle on Friday. How many times Stefan Castle has the ball and Randle just lets him go right by him. The Julius Randle performance on Friday was nauseating. And hey, like to me, he's a top the list, right? We can discuss other guys at times, the moodiness, you know, how frank some of those film sessions have been, you know, throughout the course of the year, heck going back multiple years. I mean, those things get vocal. I'd love to sit in on a Chris Finch film session. I really would. He lights those guys up. The beauty is, especially somebody like Ant, can take it. You can mother F these guys. Julius? Not so much.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Julius Randle's sensitive nature makes him the most likely trade candidate this summer
quotes.excerpt: How long have we discussed the sensitive nature of Julius Randle? ... If I had to bet on anybody being traded this summer, it's Julius Randle.
quotes.quote: How long have we discussed the sensitive nature of Julius Randle? Just look at the numbers post-trade deadline. He was absolutely impacted. He knew if Giannis ends up here, he's elsewhere. He went to ownership. He was vocal. No, this is where I want to be. Please don't trade me. But then you would think you would back that up. They don't trade him. He didn't back it up. Now, do I think Rudy Gobert can be moody at times, some other guys, but like these guys see how hard Rudy works. Look at Rudy's body. Nobody's questioning Rudy's desire. Maybe at times, temperamental, whatever, but like Rudy opens up his house after one of the Denver games. He's like, Aio, you know, and Aio actually shouted it out how Rudy said, hey, come on over. Rudy's invested hundreds of thousands of dollars in recovery equipment, right? So at Rudy's house in the West Metro, he's got any number of contraptions where like you can get your body right. And Aio gets here and Rudy's like, come on over, Aio. My house is your house, right? There's a warmth there with Rudy. So I'm not suggesting Rudy can't be moody, but like to me, when Naz Reid is alluding to the moodiness of this team, Phil, it's Julius Randle front and center. And if I had to bet on anybody being traded this summer, it's Julius Randle.

quotes.speaker: Darren Wolfson
quotes.summary_phrase: Julius Randle's pathetic effort in the playoffs signals it's time to move on
quotes.excerpt: Watch back in the first quarter his effort. Just watch it back from Friday. It was as pathetic as it gets.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I just watch back. Like just key in on him, watch back in the first quarter his effort. Just watch it back from Friday. It was as pathetic as it gets. And we discussed last Tuesday, hey, how this series goes the rest of the way will hinge a lot on how Julius plays. Well, Julius stunk in Game 5, he stunk in Game 6, he stunk for the duration of the series, but I also don't want to take away from Julius's brilliance last year. Like think about how good he was against the Lakers. How good he was against the Warriors. He had one good game, or maybe it was two, against OKC. He was so good coming back from that injury last year. So I don't want to diminish a lot of what Julius has accomplished here. But the time is now that you move on from Julius Randle.
